archetypes.name: Read a Quadratic Form
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.1 — Quadratic Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: A quadratic function has a parabolic graph whose opening, vertex, axis, intercepts, and extrema follow from its coefficients and form.
archetypes.mentalModel: Read the form first: the leading coefficient sets opening, vertex form reveals the turning point, and symmetry organizes the graph around its axis.
archetypes.governingRelation: f(x)=a(x-h)^2+k; vertex=(h,k); axis x=h; a>0 minimum, a<0 maximum

cognitiveTraps.description: Reading the sign inside (x-h) as the vertex coordinate instead of solving x-h=0.
Reporting the x-coordinate of the vertex when the question asks for the minimum or maximum output.
Reversing whether a positive or negative leading coefficient opens up or down.

figureBuilders.title: A quadratic graph is symmetric about its vertex

archetypes.name: Find a Vertex from General Form
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.1 — Quadratic Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: For f(x)=ax^2+bx+c, the vertex lies on x=-b/(2a), and its output is found by evaluating the function there.
archetypes.mentalModel: First locate the symmetry axis from the coefficient ratio; then substitute that input into the whole function to find the turning-point output.

cognitiveTraps.description: Using -b/a instead of -b/(2a) for the axis.
Stopping after finding the vertex input when the question asks for the minimum or maximum value.
Substituting the vertex input into only one term rather than the entire polynomial.

figureBuilders.title: The vertex lies on the axis of symmetry

archetypes.name: State a Quadratic Domain and Range
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.1 — Quadratic Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: A polynomial quadratic has all real inputs unless context restricts them; its outputs begin at a minimum or end at a maximum determined by the vertex.
archetypes.mentalModel: Use the variable that represents inputs for the domain, then use the vertex output and opening direction to set the range endpoint.
archetypes.governingRelation: domain=(-∞,∞) for an unrestricted quadratic; a>0 => range=[k,∞); a<0 => range=(-∞,k]

cognitiveTraps.description: Applying the vertex's output restriction to inputs or reporting all real outputs.
Choosing the wrong closed endpoint direction based on whether the parabola opens up or down.
Using a strict endpoint even though the vertex value is attained.

args.title: The vertex sets the included range endpoint

figureBuilders.title: A quadratic's range includes its vertex value

archetypes.name: Optimize a Quadratic Model
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.1 — Quadratic Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: A quadratic model that opens downward has a maximum at its vertex; a feasible context can restrict which inputs are meaningful.
archetypes.mentalModel: Translate the situation into one variable, check the model's feasible input interval, and report both the input where the extreme occurs and its output value.
archetypes.governingRelation: A(x)=ax^2+bx+c; x_vertex=-b/(2a); maximum=A(x_vertex) when a<0 and x_vertex is feasible

cognitiveTraps.description: Reporting the input where the maximum occurs as the maximum value itself.
Using a vertex outside the context's permitted input interval.
Treating the vertex of a downward-opening parabola as a minimum.

usedContexts: A rectangular garden abuts an existing wall, so only three sides need fencing. The two sides perpendicular to the wall have equal width.
